correctness.rationale: The explicit majority transition for two distinguished bits, m ordinary a-shore bits and b-shore population is exact. An initially mixed b-shore cannot be regenerated after any uniformization; recurrence forces it to be fixed and the a-shore to have exactly a/2 ones. The even-b half-balance case swaps the distinguished bits; the odd-b central two levels apply AND/OR and have only the a=4 balanced fixed anomaly. A uniform b-shore forces uniform a-shore, yielding only the two consensus states and the opposite-shore two-cycle. This exhausts fixed states and 2-cycles for every a,b>=3. Independent explicit labelled enumeration tested 1,024,064 states, and a separate weighted signature checker tested 1,681 parameter pairs. All-size proof is symbolic and does not rest on finite tests.

value.rationale: The result classifies a natural infinite two-parameter minimal edge perturbation and proves a sharp parity-dependent conversion of central-binomial numbers of equilibria into oscillatory orbits while conserving the total recurrent population. It also identifies a genuinely different fixed-point anomaly at the smallest even shore with at least three vertices. These exact dynamical invariants are not routine consequences of a finite period bound and have a motivated role in sensitivity of binary threshold networks.
